headline: The US energy regulator FERC has largely rejected a plan by PJM Interconnection, the largest US grid operator, that would have let new data centers connect without bringing matching power in return for accepting cuts before grid emergencies.
score_reason: Ruling is dated 9 Oct 2026 and was widely reported on 12 Oct, so it is stale for the 13 Oct window; lowered 2 from 8.
importance_line: Households and businesses in PJM's region keep the risk of higher power prices and still have no agreed rule on who is cut off first in a shortage, data center developers lose a quick route onto the grid, and it is unclear whether states or a revised PJM plan will fill the gap.
summary: Utility Dive reports that FERC ruled on 9 Oct 2026 that PJM's scheme, which would have let large users connect if they accept being curtailed (cut off) before emergencies, intrudes on state control of retail electricity and appears to discriminate against big users, while approving a registry of large loads. Analysts at Jefferies quoted by Utility Dive say the ruling could keep capacity prices higher for longer, which would favor power producers.
notes: Read Utility Dive because The Hill is blocked (HTTP 403); Reuters, The Dominion Post and others carried the ruling on 12 and 13 Oct. Ruling dated 9 Oct 2026.
